evidence.quote: A mechanical alloying process was carried out on a high energy ball mill (Retsch PM4) with a selected rotation speed of 250 rpm. After ball milling, multi-element alloy powder with a unitary FCC structure was formed.

process_steps.input_state: multi-element alloy powder mixed with WC powder

evidence.quote: The mixing process was carried out in a high energy ball mill with a selected rotation speed of 250 rpm for 48 h.

The wet ball milling process was carried out in a low energy ball mill with a rotation speed of 400 rpm for 2 h. After wet ball milling, the powder mixtures were taken from the vial and dried at 80 °C.
The granulated powder was compacted at a pressure of 100 MPa to form a disk of 12 mm in diameter and up to about 4 mm in height.
After press forming, the admixed powders were debound at 500 °C and then liquid-phase sintered at 1300 –1450 °C.

In this study, we found that WC grain growth can be considerably inhibited by the multi-element alloy.

Accordingly, the hardness of WC/Co composite can be reduced by the WC grain growth. When the composite is comprised of the same binder metal, the hardness of WC/multi-element composite is higher than WC/Co composite.
This phenomenon can be attributed to three factors: (1) the hardness of multi-element alloy is higher than Co;
